The blade had a total of 172 film-cooling holes in 8 rows, with 3 staggered rows of compound-angled shower-head holes.
The film-cooling holes had a diameter of 0.381 mm, which was about 1% of the blade axial chord at mid-span.
The multi-block grid had a total of 2,205,760 cells, with 80 control volumes within each hole exit.
The heat transfer coefficient was highest in the leading edge region and the tip region of the cooled blade.
The film cooling effectiveness was lowest in the leading edge region and near the tip, especially over the suction surface.
The heat transfer coefficient on the cooled blade was generally lower than that on the uncooled blade, except in the shower-head region and the tip region on the suction side.
The heat transfer coefficient was much higher on the shroud compared to the hub for both the cooled and uncooled cases.
The blowing parameter (Br) varied from row to row, with a value of 0.3393 for row 1, 0.357 for row 2, and 0.19 for the three staggered shower-head rows (3, 4, and 5).
The computed and given coolant mass flow rates matched very well, with the total coolant mass flow rate for the three staggered shower-head rows (3, 4, and 5) being the same as the given value.
Gridding the tip clearance gap, instead of using a tip clearance model, resulted in only minor changes to the heat transfer coefficient and effectiveness distributions on the blade surface.
The k-omega turbulence model of Wilcox with Menter's modifications was used for modeling the turbulence.
The multi-block grid was generated using the GridPro/az3000 software, with the viscous grid having over 2.2 million cells.
The hole exits were discretized with 80 control volumes each to capture the coolant flow details.
The low effectiveness regions were found to be in the leading edge region and near the tip, especially over the suction surface.
The high heat transfer coefficient regions were in the leading edge region and the tip region of the cooled blade.
